myopia.abstract: Myopia represents a failure of the normal process of emmetropization, which is essentially endogenous to the eye. Emmetropization involves defocus detection at the level of the amacrine and bipolar cells of the outer retina, diffusion of a signal or signals across the retinal pigment epithelium and choroid, and alteration of the scleral matrix, likely through modulation of proteoglycan synthesis. myopia.abstract: Myopia is a significant public health problem and its prevalence may be increasing over time. The main treatment options of single vision spectacle lenses, contact lenses, and refractive surgery do not slow the accompanying eye growth or retard the physiological changes associated with excessive axial elongation. High myopia is a predisposing factor for retinal detachment, myopic retinopathy, and glaucoma, contributing to loss of vision and blindness. myopia.abstract: The aim was to determine how visual acuity is affected by myopia when optical factors of the eye are controlled. Grating acuity was measured with interference fringes to avoid the effects of aberrations, and ocular biometry was used to compensate for differences in retinal image size among subjects. Distance spectacle refractions ranged from +2.25 to -14.75 D. The retinal magnification factor (RMF) in mm/deg was computed for each eye from the distance refraction, central corneal power and ultrasound biometry. A forced-choice orientation discrimination method was used to measure acuity for high-contrast 543 nm laser interference fringes in three retinal locations: the fovea, and at 4 deg and 10 deg eccentricity in the temporal retina. Acuity, expressed in c/deg and adjusted for spectacle magnification, was not significantly correlated with refraction at any of the three retinal locations.

myopia.abstract: Current knowledge of the refractive shifts (twilight myopia, night myopia, dark focus) that occur as the luminance is progressively lowered from photopic levels is reviewed. In complete darkness, myopic changes of the order of 1 dioptre are typical in young adult subjects. These gradually diminish as presbyopia is approached. The possible role of these refractive changes in causing visual difficulties for young drivers on the road at night is considered. myopia.abstract: The effect of myopic defocus on myopia progression was assessed in a two-year prospective study on 94 myopes aged 9-14 years, randomly allocated to an undercorrected group or a fully corrected control group. The 47 experimental subjects were blurred by approximately +0.75 D (blurring VA to 6/12), while the controls were fully corrected. Undercorrection produced more rapid myopia progression and axial elongation (ANOVA, F(1,374)=14.32, p<0.01). Contrary to animal studies, myopic defocus speeds up myopia development in already myopic humans. Myopia could be caused by a failure to detect the direction of defocus rather than by a mechanism exhibiting a zero-point error.

myopia.abstract: The relationship between accommodative lag and annual myopia progression was investigated using linear models in 592 myopic children wearing a full refractive correction in the Collaborative Longitudinal Evaluation of Ethnicity and Refractive Error (CLEERE) Study. The mean (± SD) age and spherical equivalent refractive error at baseline were 10.4 ± 1.8 years and -2.13 ± 1.24 D, respectively. The mean annual progression of myopia was -0.45 ± 0.32 D, and the mean accommodative lag (for a 4-D Badal stimulus) was 1.59 ± 0.63 D. Neither lag at the beginning nor at the end of a yearly progression interval was associated with annual myopia progression (all p ≥ 0.12). These data suggest that foveal hyperopic retinal blur during near viewing may not drive juvenile-onset myopia progression.

myopia.summary: LASIK is contraindicated in patients with Avellino corneal dystrophy because vision may be reduced by corneal opacities that appear in the interface of the flap and remaining posterior stroma postoperatively.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To report a case of Avellino corneal dystrophy that increased in severity 1 year after uncomplicated laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) for myopia. METHODS: Avellino dystrophy was confirmed by polymerase chain reaction sequencing of DNA from the patient and her parents. RESULTS: Best spectacle-corrected visual acuity decreased from 20/20 to 20/30 12 to 20 months after LASIK owing to opacities that appeared centrally in the corneal stroma and the LASIK flap and remaining posterior stroma interface. CONCLUSIONS: LASIK is contraindicated in patients with Avellino corneal dystrophy because vision may be reduced by corneal opacities that appear in the interface of the flap and remaining posterior stroma postoperatively.

myopia.abstract: The choroid of the eye is primarily a vascular structure supplying the outer retina. myopia.summary: Hantaviruses are enzootic viruses that maintain persistent infections in their rodent hosts without apparent disease symptoms. The spillover of these viruses to humans can lead to one of two serious illnesses, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. …
myopia.abstract: Hantaviruses are enzootic viruses that maintain persistent infections in their rodent hosts without apparent disease symptoms. The spillover of these viruses to humans can lead to one of two serious illnesses, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. In recent years, there has been an improved understanding of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and natural history of these viruses following an increase in the number of outbreaks in the Americas. In this review, current concepts regarding the ecology of and disease associated with these serious human pathogens are presented. Priorities for future research suggest an integration of the ecology and evolution of these and other host-virus ecosystems through modeling and hypothesis-driven research with the risk of emergence, host switching/spillover, and disease transmission to humans.

myopia.abstract: Hantaviruses are carried by numerous rodent species throughout the world. In 1993, a previously unknown group of hantaviruses emerged in the United States as the cause of an acute respiratory disease now termed hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). Before than, hantaviruses were known as the etiologic agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, a disease that occurs almost entirely in the Eastern Hemisphere. Since the discovery of the HPS-causing hantaviruses, intense investigation of the ecology and epidemiology of hantaviruses has led to the discovery of many other novel hantaviruses. Their ubiquity and potential for causing severe human illness make these viruses an important public health concern; we reviewed the distribution, ecology, disease potential, and genetic spectrum.

myopia.abstract: The history, taxonomy, geographic distribution, clinical disease, and therapy of the pathogenic nonpigmented or late-pigmenting rapidly growing mycobacteria (RGM) are reviewed. Community-acquired disease and health care-associated disease are highlighted for each species. The latter grouping includes health care-associated outbreaks and pseudo-outbreaks as well as sporadic disease cases. Treatment recommendations for each species and type of disease are also described. Special emphasis is on the Mycobacterium fortuitum group, including M. fortuitum, M. peregrinum, and the unnamed third biovariant complex with its recent taxonomic changes and newly recognized species (including M. septicum, M. mageritense, and proposed species M. houstonense and M. bonickei). myopia.abstract: The major challenge faced by today's pharmacologist and formulation scientist is ocular drug delivery. Topical eye drop is the most convenient and patient compliant route of drug administration, especially for the treatment of anterior segment diseases. Delivery of drugs to the targeted ocular tissues is restricted by various precorneal, dynamic and static ocular barriers. Also, therapeutic drug levels are not maintained for longer duration in target tissues. In the past two decades, ocular drug delivery research acceleratedly advanced towards developing a novel, safe and patient compliant formulation and drug delivery devices/techniques, which may surpass these barriers and maintain drug levels in tissues. contactlens.abstract: Contact lens wearers are often noncompliant with use of their multipurpose solutions, and eye care practitioners infrequently recommend the use of hydrogen peroxide solutions. A novel contact lens disinfection and cleaning system has been created to disinfect and remove deposits using electrolysis with electrophoresis technology. The system can be used to clean soft, corneal rigid gas-permeable, and scleral contact lenses. Independent laboratory testing demonstrated that 30-minutes of enhanced cleaning with the device reduced the number of microbial colonies to "below detectable" for Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Candida albicans and Fusarium solani. This study evaluated the influence of contact lens material and back vertex power (BVP) on handling characteristics in soft daily disposable contact lenses. Current DED management emphasizes identifying the patient's predominant etiological contributors and tailoring treatment accordingly. While aphakia in adults is primarily managed through intraocular lens (IOL) implantation, the use of IOLs in children is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration, and IOL implantation is particularly controversial in infants. Therefore, contact lenses (CLs) have an important role to play in the management of pediatric aphakia. In light of evolving regional lens availability, this narrative review aims to provide practical guidance, clinical pearls, and regional insights on CL choice and to discuss unmet needs in the management of pediatric aphakia, drawing on both contemporary evidence and expert testimony. contactlens.abstract: This review delineates the spatial distribution of ocular surface microbiota (OSM) and its dynamic interplay with ocular health. Culture-independent surveys employing 16S rRNA and metagenomic sequencing reveal an ultra-low-biomass ecosystem characterized by restricted α-diversity. Firmicutes, Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria are the dominant phyla. Corynebacterium, coagulase-negative staphylococci, Propionibacterium and Streptococcus show high prevalence and temporal stability. These four genera form a conserved core. Their relative abundance is continuously reshaped by geography, lifestyle, age, sex, delivery mode, contact lens wear and systemic diseases such as dry eye and diabetes. contactlens.abstract: Scleral lens practitioners frequently observe that the limbal fit of contemporary scleral lens designs is suboptimal. Inadequate limbal fit can lead to adverse corneal health findings, including limbal staining, limbal microcysts, conjunctival prolapse, neovascularisation, and limbal stem cell deficiency. These complications may compromise patient comfort and long-term corneal health, potentially affecting limbal stem cells through hypoxic or mechanical stress. Consequently, they may affect the long-term suitability for scleral lens wear of the patient and require the practitioner to carefully assess the risks and benefits of continued use. contactlens.summary: Future studies should prioritize direct comparisons of novel platforms with standard therapy and establish whether improved delivery maintains concentrations above pathogen-specific inhibitory thresholds and translates into superior clinical outcomes.
contactlens.abstract: PURPOSE: Infectious keratitis remains a leading cause of corneal blindness worldwide despite effective antimicrobial agents. Conventional topical therapy is limited by rapid precorneal clearance, restricted corneal penetration, and inadequate stromal drug exposure, resulting in subtherapeutic drug concentrations. These pharmacokinetic barriers are particularly important in fungal, protozoal, deep stromal, and antimicrobial-resistant keratitis, where prolonged or targeted exposure is essential for successful treatment. This review evaluates emerging ocular antimicrobial delivery strategies through a pharmacokinetic framework, emphasizing the relationship among delivery platform, depth of corneal involvement, pathogen-specific requirements, and clinical feasibility. contactlens.abstract: Micro- and nano-plastics (MNPs) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants originating from the degradation of plastics and direct release from consumer products. Global plastic production is projected to nearly double by 2050, intensifying human exposure through inhalation, ingestion, and direct ocular contact. This review synthesizes current evidence on the presence, distribution, and health impacts of MNPs in human ocular tissues, their toxicological effects in animal and cellular models, underlying pathological mechanisms, and contributions from ophthalmic materials. contactlens.abstract: The ocular surface microenvironment (OSM), which is regulated by the lacrimal functional unit and the external environment, is highly dynamic and determines the health of the ocular surface (OS). Descriptive, comparative, and multivariable analyses were performed to examine ocular symptoms and their associations with contact lens use and relevant participant characteristics. RESULTS: A total of 408 students participated, of whom 202 (49.5%) were contact lens users and 87.7% were female. contactlens.abstract: Chronic infectious keratitis represents a distinct clinical entity characterized by indolent progression, diagnostic difficulty, and prolonged therapeutic courses. Unlike acute bacterial keratitis, chronic infections often present with subtle inflammatory signs, recurrent episodes, or poor response to empirical antimicrobial therapy. Among the most important causes are herpetic keratitis, acanthamoeba keratitis, Microsporidial stromal keratitis, and atypical (non-tuberculous) mycobacterial keratitis. Herpes simplex virus keratitis may manifest as recurrent epithelial disease or immune-mediated stromal inflammation resulting from viral latency and reactivation, frequently leading to corneal scarring and neurotrophic complications. METHODS: This prospective observational study included 18 participants with keratoconus (18 study eyes). Scleral lenses were fitted bilaterally, while one eye per participant was selected for ocular analysis; when both eyes were eligible, the eye with the higher Kmax was selected. contactlens.abstract: Vision impairment is a significant global health issue, affecting people of all ages and notably influencing quality of life. One of the major challenges in treating eye diseases is the effective delivery of drugs, as the eye possesses unique anatomical and physiological barriers. Structures such as tear drainage, the tightly packed corneal epithelium, and the blood‑ocular barriers often hinder medications from reaching therapeutic concentrations. Conventional treatments such as eye drops, ointments, and oral medications frequently exhibit poor bioavailability and limited penetration into target sites, particularly in posterior segment diseases. This often leads to minimal therapeutic relief or requires frequent dosing, which can compromise patient comfort and adherence. contactlens.abstract: Regulatory agencies in the United States and abroad are increasingly citing clinics and surgical facilities for what they deem to be inadequate disinfection of Goldmann applanation tonometer (GAT) tips, gonioscopy lenses, laser lenses, and other reusable clinic devices that contact the ocular surface. These regulators require routine high-level disinfection (HLD) of these reusable devices to prevent infection transmission. A multisociety task force formed to assess the necessity of HLD found no published evidence that these devices transmit sight-threatening infections or that HLD reduces infection transmission compared with lower-level disinfection methods. contactlens.abstract: Müller muscle-conjunctival resection (MMCR) has traditionally been regarded as a posterior approach for mild-to-moderate blepharoptosis in patients with good levator function and a positive response to phenylephrine. Its contemporary role, however, is considerably broader. Accumulating evidence supports the use of MMCR in selected patients with limited or absent phenylephrine responsiveness, more severe ptosis, postoperative eyelid asymmetry, and carefully chosen congenital, neurogenic, or neuromuscular forms of ptosis. In parallel, modifications that incorporate tarsectomy, simplified suturing, conjunctiva-sparing approaches, perioperative bandage contact lenses, and targeted hemostatic maneuvers have sought to improve predictability, comfort, and safety. contactlens.title: Fungal keratitis.
contactlens.summary: Fungal keratitis, or keratomycoses, are corneal infections which must be considered in cases of corneal trauma, prior corneal surgery, chronic ocular surface disease, topical corticosteroids or contact lens wear. Filamentous fungi or yeasts may be involved. …
contactlens.abstract: Fungal keratitis, or keratomycoses, are corneal infections which must be considered in cases of corneal trauma, prior corneal surgery, chronic ocular surface disease, topical corticosteroids or contact lens wear. Filamentous fungi or yeasts may be involved. Presenting clinical features such as corneal infiltrates with feathery edges and/or raised surface, intact epithelium with deep stromal involvement, satellite lesions, endothelial plaques, lack of improvement with antibiotics and worsening with steroids are suggestive of fungal keratitis. Corneal scraping for laboratory examination is mandatory. Medical management with antifungal eye drops and systemic agents should be started as soon as possible. Surgical interventions are required in a significant number of cases to control the infection. The prognosis of fungal keratitis is worse than that of bacterial keratitis.

contactlens.abstract: Acanthamoeba keratitis (AK) is a rare protozoal infection of the cornea. At least eight species of Acanthamoeba are known to cause this sight-threatening disease of the ocular surface. Acanthamoeba spp. exist in a wide array of niches ranging from thermal springs to under ice and every conceivable habitat in between. Contact lens wear is the leading risk factor for AK and is practiced by over 30 million individuals in the United States, yet the incidence of AK is less than 33 cases per one million contact lens wearers. Serological studies have reported that 90%-100% of individuals with no history of AK possess antibodies specific for Acanthamoeba antigens indicating that exposure to this organism is commonplace, yet disease is remarkably rare. contactlens.abstract: Nowadays, keratitis, corneal infection due to wearing contact lens means an increasingly serious problem. Neglected cases may lead to corneal damage that can cause blindness in cases of otherwise healthy eyes. Early diagnosis based on the clinical picture and the typical patient history is an important way of prevention. Prophylaxis is substantial to avoid bacterial and viral infection that is highly essential in this group of diseases. Teaching contact lens wearers the proper contact lens care, storage, sterility, and hygiene regulations is of great importance. In case of corneal inflammation early accurate diagnosis supported by microbiological culture from contact lenses, storage boxes or cornea is very useful. Thereafter, targeted drug therapy or in therapy-resistant cases surgical treatment may even be necessary in order to sustain suitable visual acuity.

A variety of systemic drugs can also induce DED secondary to multiple mechanisms. Moreover, the use of contact lens induces or is associated with DED. contactlens.abstract: Contact lenses represent a widely utilized form of vision correction with more than 140 million wearers worldwide. Although generally well-tolerated, contact lenses can cause corneal infection (microbial keratitis), with an approximate annualized incidence ranging from ~2 to ~20 cases per 10,000 wearers, and sometimes resulting in permanent vision loss. Research suggests that the pathogenesis of contact lens-associated microbial keratitis is complex and multifactorial, likely requiring multiple conspiring factors that compromise the intrinsic resistance of a healthy cornea to infection. References in all relevant publications were also reviewed. contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantify tear elimination rate (ER) underneath silicone hydrogel (Si-Hy) and scleral gas permeable (GP) contact lenses (CLs). METHODS: Subjects successfully using either well-fitting soft Si-Hy CLs or scleral GP CLs were recruited. Most scleral GP CL wearers had irregular corneas (e.g., keratoconus). An objective fluorometer measured decay of fluorescein isothiocyanate dextran dye signal (70 kD MW) from which the tear ER in %/min was calculated. For GP scleral lenses, the ER was determined for both the initial settling period and the 30- to 60-min period, and without lenses. All ERs were calculated from 5 to 30 min to avoid reflex tearing effects. RESULTS: Fourteen soft Si-Hy CL and 12 scleral GP CL wearers completed the study. The ER for the scleral GP CL wearers averaged 0.57 (±0.6) %/min for the 0- to 30-min and 0.42 (±0.5) %/min for the 30- to 60-min period (P=0.515).

contactlens.abstract: Accurate and reliable monitoring of blood glucose is needed for the treatment of diabetes, which has many challenges, including lack of patient compliance. Measuring tear glucose is an alternative to traditional finger-stick tests used to track blood sugar levels, but glucose sensing using tears has yet to be achieved. We report a methodology for possible tear glucose monitoring using glucose-sensitive silicone hydrogel (SiHG) contact lenses, the primary type of lenses available in today's market. Initially, we assessed the interpenetrating polymer network, with nearly pure silicone and water regions, existing in the SiHGs using a polarity-sensitive probe Prodan. contactlens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To review the effect of contact lens (CL) material, design, and fitting characteristics on CL discomfort. METHODS: A PubMed search identified publications describing subjective comfort and CL material, fitting, and design parameters. The review included clinical signs associated with discomfort that may be a consequence of these parameters. RESULTS: Reduced lens movement or more CL tightness were associated with improved comfort. Increased lens-induced paralimbal conjunctival staining and indentation, considered as quasi-indicators of CL fitting or edge design, were also associated with better comfort. No recent studies have evaluated varying CL design parameters and subjective comfort. Silicone hydrogel CLs are no different in comfort compared with hydrogel CLs. contactlens.summary: Ocular infection is caused by both endogenous (resident) and exogenous (environmental) microbes. As the ocular surface interacts with both outer environment and its own resident microbiota, clinical ocular samples are predicted to contain a diverse set of microorganisms. …
contactlens.abstract: Ocular infection is caused by both endogenous (resident) and exogenous (environmental) microbes. As the ocular surface interacts with both outer environment and its own resident microbiota, clinical ocular samples are predicted to contain a diverse set of microorganisms. Microscopy of sample smears is an important step in the diagnostic process of infectious diseases to interpret the culture results. Traditional culture techniques have several limitations in the detection and/or identification of uncharacterized bacteria of environmental origin. Molecular biological techniques, such as polymerase chain reaction of pathogen-specific virulence genes, 16S rRNA gene clone library analysis, and next-generation sequencing of 16S rDNA amplicons, compensate for diagnostic culture techniques in diagnosing infectious diseases. These techniques are expected to provide novel insights into the ocular

contactlens.title: Contact lens hygiene compliance and lens case contamination: A review.
contactlens.summary: A contaminated contact lens case can act as a reservoir for microorganisms that could potentially compromise contact lens wear and lead to sight threatening adverse events. …
contactlens.abstract: A contaminated contact lens case can act as a reservoir for microorganisms that could potentially compromise contact lens wear and lead to sight threatening adverse events. The rate, level and profile of microbial contamination in lens cases, compliance and other risk factors associated with lens case contamination, and the challenges currently faced in this field are discussed. The rate of lens case contamination is commonly over 50%. Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, Bacillus spp., Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Serratia marcescens are frequently recovered from lens cases. In addition, we provide suggestions regarding how to clean contact lens cases and improve lens wearers' compliance as well as future lens case design for reducing lens case contamination. This review highlights the challenges in reducing the level of microbial contamination which require an industry wide approach.

contactlens.title: Multidrug resistant Fusarium keratitis.
contactlens.summary: Fusarium keratitis may progress to severe endophthalmitis. Clinical suspicion is paramount in order to start antifungal therapy without delay. Therapy is complex due to the high resistance of this organism to usual antifungal drugs.
contactlens.abstract: CASE REPORT: We report a case of keratitis in a female contact lens wearer, who developed a deep corneal abscess. The culture of a corneal biopsy scraping was positive for multiresistant Fusarium solani. The patient has a complicated clinical course and failed to respond to local and systemic antifungal treatment, requiring eye enucleation. CONCLUSION: Fusarium keratitis may progress to severe endophthalmitis. Clinical suspicion is paramount in order to start antifungal therapy without delay. Therapy is complex due to the high resistance of this organism to usual antifungal drugs.

contactlens.title: The diagnosis and management of contact lens-related microbial keratitis.
contactlens.summary: Contact lens-associated microbial keratitis poses a diagnostic dilemma for optometrists on two fronts. The distinction between sterile inflammation and microbial infection is often blurred. …
contactlens.abstract: Contact lens-associated microbial keratitis poses a diagnostic dilemma for optometrists on two fronts. The distinction between sterile inflammation and microbial infection is often blurred. In addition, there is a requirement with nearly 50 per cent of the Australian and New Zealand optometric profession being therapeutically endorsed, to distinguish between cases of infection that can be managed in the community verses those that require escalation to public hospitals that have access to laboratory diagnostic tools and advanced imaging techniques, such as in vivo confocal microscopy. Pattern recognition and incorporation of knowledge of aetiology and risk factors assists optometrists to decide on optimal management strategies. Skilled optometrists will utilise emerging diagnostic and therapeutic technologies to ensure safe management strategies and better outcomes for these cases.

METHODS: Retrospective review of corneal ulcer cases identified by search of the ophthalmology and microbiology department databases between 1999 and 2016. RESULTS: Six hundred seventy-seven cases of corneal ulcers were identified, of which 46% were CLRU. Conjunctival injection is most commonly caused by dryness, allergy, visual fatigue, contact lens overwear, and local infections. …
contactlens.abstract: "Red eye" is used as a general term to describe irritated or bloodshot eyes. It is a recognizable sign of an acute/chronic, localized/systemic underlying inflammatory condition. Conjunctival injection is most commonly caused by dryness, allergy, visual fatigue, contact lens overwear, and local infections. In some instances, red eye can represent a true ocular emergency that should be treated by an ophthalmologist. A comprehensive assessment of red eye conditions is required to preserve the patients visual function. Severe ocular pain, significant photophobia, decreased vision, and history of ocular trauma are warning signs demanding immediate ophthalmological consultation.

In tropical and subtropical areas, the infection is relatively common and associated with trauma or chronic eye diseases. contactlens.title: Regional spread of contact lens-related Acanthamoeba keratitis in Italy.
contactlens.summary: Acanthamoeba ocular infections, known as Acanthamoeba keratitis, are an emerging problem among contact lens wearers. Infections mediated by Acanthamoeba are uncommon, but they can be underestimated due to poor awareness and delayed diagnosis. …
contactlens.abstract: Acanthamoeba ocular infections, known as Acanthamoeba keratitis, are an emerging problem among contact lens wearers. Infections mediated by Acanthamoeba are uncommon, but they can be underestimated due to poor awareness and delayed diagnosis. The routine use of rapid and cost-effective molecular methods like Real Time PCR for the diagnosis of this important pathogen could improve diagnosis and therapy outcome. This report describes the detection by Real Time PCR assay of six T4 and one T3 Acanthamoeba infections, as the first reported cases in Tuscany, Italy.

contactlens.abstract: Understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms of the corneal tissue and translating them into effective therapies requires organotypic culture systems that can better model the physiological conditions of the front of the eye. Human corneal in vitro models currently exist, however, the lack of tear replenishment limits corneal in vitro models' ability to accurately simulate the physiological environment of the human cornea. The TRS is capable of generating adjustable intermittent flow from 0.1 µL in every cycle. The TRS is a sterilizable device that is designed to fit standard 6-well cell culture plates. METHODS: The authors performed a literature research for articles, published on PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus and Embase online library, relevant to pediatric keratitis etiology, risk factors, antibiotic susceptibilities, treatment and outcomes. RESULTS: Contact lens wear does induce discomfort, which is a mild form of pain, and wearing of lenses can induce increases in limbal and conjunctival redness. Such outbreaks are the result of lapses in contact lens wear and care and of alterations in water quality and water treatment procedures. …
contactlens.abstract: The occurrence of Acanthamoeba keratitis is increasing in the United States because of an expanding population at risk of infection and sporadic outbreaks of infection. Such outbreaks are the result of lapses in contact lens wear and care and of alterations in water quality and water treatment procedures. Although improved techniques in diagnosis are available, better identification of infection alone does not explain an increase in the observed occurrence of the disease. Likewise, there does not appear to be an increase in the virulence or infectivity of the amoebae. Strategies for prevention, including patient education, improved decontaminating agents, maintenance of water treatment standards, and possible immunization of subjects at risk, are needed.

RESULTS: High Dk silicone hydrogel contact lenses became available for research and clinical practice almost 10 and 5 years ago respectively. During that time many studies have been conducted and it has been demonstrated repeatedly how much improvement there has been to the physiological response of the eye particularly when wearing the lenses on an overnight basis. This article summarizes current knowledge of the estimates and determinants of risk associated with re-useable hydrogel lenses and discusses study design considerations for future studies. The absolute risk of microbial keratitis to the wearer has been remarkably stable since 1989. contactlens.title: An early assessment of silicone hydrogel safety: pearls and pitfalls, and current status.
contactlens.summary: The contact lens industry has evolved and now provides many choices, including continuous wear, overnight orthokeratology, frequent-replacement lenses, daily-disposable lenses, and many alternatives in systems of care and maintenance. …
contactlens.abstract: The contact lens industry has evolved and now provides many choices, including continuous wear, overnight orthokeratology, frequent-replacement lenses, daily-disposable lenses, and many alternatives in systems of care and maintenance. Epidemiologic studies to date have shown that how a lens is worn, particularly if worn overnight, can increase the risk of microbial keratitis. However, the risk of silicone hydrogel contact lenses worn on a continuous-wear basis has been evaluated only recently. This article summarizes the recent research data on extended-wear silicone hydrogel lenses and discusses the challenges of early evaluations of silicone hydrogel lens safety. Finally, the relevance of this information is discussed to practitioners and contact lens wearers making choices about the risks and benefits of different products and how they are used.

contactlens.abstract: The tear film is a complex fluid that is precisely maintained and which is essential to the health of the ocular surface. One of the major components of the tear film is lipid, which is produced by the meibomian glands and serves many important functions on the ocular surface. It is estimated that there are more than 45 individual lipids within the tear film, which vary greatly in their structure and properties. The composition of the lipid within the tear film has an enormous influence on the stability of the tear film, with a subsequent impact on the occurrence of dry eye and the ultimate success of contact lens wear. Recent outbreaks of unusual adverse events related to multifaceted issues of lens wear, compliance and lens care, have led to a systematic review of contact lenses and their relationship to the ocular environment. contactlens.title: Surface wettability enhancement of silicone hydrogel lenses by processing with polar plastic molds.
contactlens.summary: In the quest for hydrogel contact lenses with improved extended wear capability, the use of siloxane moieties in the lens materials was investigated. However, the introduction of hydrophobic siloxane groups gave rise to wettability and lipidlike deposit problems. …
contactlens.abstract: In the quest for hydrogel contact lenses with improved extended wear capability, the use of siloxane moieties in the lens materials was investigated. However, the introduction of hydrophobic siloxane groups gave rise to wettability and lipidlike deposit problems. It was found that when polysiloxane-based compositions for hydrogels were processed with polar plastic molds, such as those fabricated from an acrylonitrile-based polymer, the hydrogel lenses fabricated were wettable, with minimized lipidlike deposits. These findings were supported by the wettability of silicone hydrogel films, silicon, and nitrogen element contents near lens surfaces, as well as the results from clinical assessment of silicone hydrogel lenses.

contactlens.abstract: Though biofilms were first described by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, the theory describing the biofilm process was not developed until 1978. We now understand that biofilms are universal, occurring in aquatic and industrial water systems as well as a large number of environments and medical devices relevant for public health. Using tools such as the scanning electron microscope and, more recently, the confocal laser scanning microscope, biofilm researchers now understand that biofilms are not unstructured, homogeneous deposits of cells and accumulated slime, but complex communities of surface-associated cells enclosed in a polymer matrix containing open water channels. Further studies have shown that the biofilm phenotype can be described in terms of the genes expressed by biofilm-associated cells. contactlens.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are of concern because of their high persistence (or that of their degradation products) and their impacts on human and environmental health that are known or can be deduced from some well-studied PFAS. Currently, many different PFAS (on the order of several thousands) are used in a wide range of applications, and there is no comprehensive source of information on the many individual substances and their functions in different applications. Here we provide a broad overview of many use categories where PFAS have been employed and for which function; we also specify which PFAS have been used and discuss the magnitude of the uses. Despite being non-exhaustive, our study clearly demonstrates that PFAS are used in almost all industry branches and many consumer products. contactlens.title: Strategies for combating bacterial biofilms: A focus on anti-biofilm agents and their mechanisms of action
contactlens.summary: Biofilm refers to the complex, sessile communities of microbes found either attached to a surface or buried firmly in an extracellular matrix as aggregates. The biofilm matrix surrounding bacteria makes them tolerant to harsh conditions and resistant to antibacterial treatments. …
contactlens.abstract: Biofilm refers to the complex, sessile communities of microbes found either attached to a surface or buried firmly in an extracellular matrix as aggregates. The biofilm matrix surrounding bacteria makes them tolerant to harsh conditions and resistant to antibacterial treatments. Moreover, the biofilms are responsible for causing a broad range of chronic diseases and due to the emergence of antibiotic resistance in bacteria it has really become difficult to treat them with efficacy. Furthermore, the antibiotics available till date are ineffective for treating these biofilm related infections due to their higher values of minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), which may result in in-vivo toxicity. Hence, it is critically important to design or screen anti-biofilm molecules that can effectively minimize and eradicate biofilm related infections.

contactlens.title: A review on polymeric hydrogel membranes for wound dressing applications: PVA-based hydrogel dressings
contactlens.summary: This review presents the past and current efforts with a brief description on the featured properties of hydrogel membranes fabricated from biopolymers and synthetic ones for wound dressing applications. …
contactlens.abstract: This review presents the past and current efforts with a brief description on the featured properties of hydrogel membranes fabricated from biopolymers and synthetic ones for wound dressing applications. Many endeavors have been exerted during past ten years for developing new artificial polymeric membranes, which fulfill the demanded conditions for the treatment of skin wounds. This review mainly focuses on representing specifications of ideal polymeric wound dressing membranes, such as crosslinked hydrogels compatible with wound dressing purposes. But as the hydrogels with single component have low mechanical strength, recent trends have offered composite or hybrid hydrogel membranes to achieve the typical wound dressing requirements.

contactlens.title: Biofilms and device-associated infections
contactlens.summary: Microorganisms commonly attach to living and nonliving surfaces, including those of indwelling medical devices, and form biofilms made up of extracellular polymers. In this state, microorganisms are highly resistant to antimicrobial treatment and are tenaciously bound to the surface. …
contactlens.abstract: Microorganisms commonly attach to living and nonliving surfaces, including those of indwelling medical devices, and form biofilms made up of extracellular polymers. In this state, microorganisms are highly resistant to antimicrobial treatment and are tenaciously bound to the surface. To better understand and control biofilms on indwelling medical devices, researchers should develop reliable sampling and measurement techniques, investigate the role of biofilms in antimicrobial drug resistance, and establish the link between biofilm contamination and patient infection.

contactlens.summary: In humans, microbial cells (including bacteria, archaea, and fungi) greatly outnumber host cells. Candida albicans is the most prevalent fungal species of the human microbiota; this species asymptomatically colonizes many areas of the body, particularly the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts of healthy individuals. …
contactlens.abstract: In humans, microbial cells (including bacteria, archaea, and fungi) greatly outnumber host cells. Candida albicans is the most prevalent fungal species of the human microbiota; this species asymptomatically colonizes many areas of the body, particularly the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts of healthy individuals. Alterations in host immunity, stress, resident microbiota, and other factors can lead to C. albicans overgrowth, causing a wide range of infections, from superficial mucosal to hematogenously disseminated candidiasis. To date, most studies of C. albicans have been carried out in suspension cultures; however, the medical impact of C. albicans (like that of many other microorganisms) depends on its ability to thrive as a biofilm, a closely packed community of cells. contactlens.title: TFOS DEWS II Tear Film Report
contactlens.summary: The members of the Tear Film Subcommittee reviewed the role of the tear film in dry eye disease (DED). The Subcommittee reviewed biophysical and biochemical aspects of tears and how these change in DED. …
contactlens.abstract: The members of the Tear Film Subcommittee reviewed the role of the tear film in dry eye disease (DED). The Subcommittee reviewed biophysical and biochemical aspects of tears and how these change in DED. Clinically, DED is characterized by loss of tear volume, more rapid breakup of the tear film and increased evaporation of tears from the ocular surface. The tear film is composed of many substances including lipids, proteins, mucins and electrolytes. All of these contribute to the integrity of the tear film but exactly how they interact is still an area of active research. Tear film osmolarity increases in DED. Changes to other components such as proteins and mucins can be used as biomarkers for DED. contactlens.title: Bacterial biofilm formation on implantable devices and approaches to its treatment and prevention
contactlens.summary: In living organisms, biofilms are defined as complex communities of bacteria residing within an exopolysaccharide matrix that adheres to a surface. In the clinic, they are typically the cause of chronic, nosocomial, and medical device-related infections. …
contactlens.abstract: In living organisms, biofilms are defined as complex communities of bacteria residing within an exopolysaccharide matrix that adheres to a surface. In the clinic, they are typically the cause of chronic, nosocomial, and medical device-related infections. Due to the antibiotic-resistant nature of biofilms, the use of antibiotics alone is ineffective for treating biofilm-related infections. In this review, we present a brief overview of concepts of bacterial biofilm formation, and current state-of-the-art therapeutic approaches for preventing and treating biofilms. Also, we have reviewed the prevalence of such infections on medical devices and discussed the future challenges that need to be overcome in order to successfully treat biofilms using the novel technologies being developed.

contactlens.title: Hydrogels: Properties and Applications in Biomedicine
contactlens.summary: Hydrogels are crosslinked polymer chains with three-dimensional (3D) network structures, which can absorb relatively large amounts of fluid. Because of the high water content, soft structure, and porosity of hydrogels, they closely resemble living tissues. …
contactlens.abstract: Hydrogels are crosslinked polymer chains with three-dimensional (3D) network structures, which can absorb relatively large amounts of fluid. Because of the high water content, soft structure, and porosity of hydrogels, they closely resemble living tissues. Research in recent years shows that hydrogels have been applied in various fields, such as agriculture, biomaterials, the food industry, drug delivery, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. Along with the underlying technology improvements of hydrogel development, hydrogels can be expected to be applied in more fields. contactlens.title: Wearable sensors: modalities, challenges, and prospects
contactlens.summary: Wearable sensors have recently seen a large increase in both research and commercialization. However, success in wearable sensors has been a mix of both progress and setbacks. Most of commercial progress has been in smart adaptation of existing mechanical, electrical and optical methods of measuring the body. …
contactlens.abstract: Wearable sensors have recently seen a large increase in both research and commercialization. However, success in wearable sensors has been a mix of both progress and setbacks. Most of commercial progress has been in smart adaptation of existing mechanical, electrical and optical methods of measuring the body. This adaptation has involved innovations in how to miniaturize sensing technologies, how to make them conformal and flexible, and in the development of companion software that increases the value of the measured data. However, chemical sensing modalities have experienced greater challenges in commercial adoption, especially for non-invasive chemical sensors. contactlens.title: Technology Roadmap for Flexible Sensors
contactlens.summary: Humans rely increasingly on sensors to address grand challenges and to improve quality of life in the era of digitalization and big data. For ubiquitous sensing, flexible sensors are developed to overcome the limitations of conventional rigid counterparts. …
contactlens.abstract: Humans rely increasingly on sensors to address grand challenges and to improve quality of life in the era of digitalization and big data. For ubiquitous sensing, flexible sensors are developed to overcome the limitations of conventional rigid counterparts. Despite rapid advancement in bench-side research over the last decade, the market adoption of flexible sensors remains limited. To ease and to expedite their deployment, here, we identify bottlenecks hindering the maturation of flexible sensors and propose promising solutions. lens.title: Global Prevalence and Risk Factors of Digital Eye Strain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
lens.summary: Digital eye strain imposes a higher disease burden in the AFR, LICs and among university students. More representative regional and population studies are needed to guide targeted prevention and interventions for high-risk groups.
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Comprehensive data on the global prevalence of digital eye strain and its associated risk factors remain scarce. This study aimed to estimate the global prevalence of digital eye strain and its associated risk factors. METHODS: CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, CBM, PubMed, Embase, WoS, and Cochrane were searched through July 2026 for studies on digital eye strain prevalence and risk factors. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed bias, and pooled estimates were calculated using fixed- and random-effects models. RESULTS: A total of 11,254 individuals with digital eye strain were included. The meta-analysis revealed a global prevalence of digital eye strain of 63%. Although the North-American (NA)/American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) and Growth and ROP (G-ROP) criteria are highly sensitive, they may trigger unnecessary examinations. lens.title: Presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses: selecting the right patient and managing dysphotopsia and neuroadaptation.
lens.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses (PrC-IOLs) offer the potential for spectacle independence across a wide range of visual distances, but postoperative satisfaction remains strongly influenced by patient selection, visual expectations, dysphotopsia, and neuroadaptation. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses (PrC-IOLs) offer the potential for spectacle independence across a wide range of visual distances, but postoperative satisfaction remains strongly influenced by patient selection, visual expectations, dysphotopsia, and neuroadaptation. This review examines recent evidence on patient selection and provides a practical approach for preventing and managing postoperative dissatisfaction. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent evidence supports a comprehensive preoperative assessment combining patient expectations and visual needs with ocular surface, corneal, refractive, retinal, and optic nerve evaluation. Selected patients with mild ocular comorbidities may achieve satisfactory outcomes, challenging rigid exclusion criteria. Photic phenomena do not necessarily result in dissatisfaction, and symptoms may improve over time through neuroadaptation.

lens.title: Impact of specialized mobility services on independent travel, economic outcomes, and well-being for people with low vision and blindness: an international survey.

lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Though independent mobility has a considerable impact on an individual's quality of life, employability, and social participation, few studies have examined the impact of specialized mobility services for people with visual impairments (PVI) globally. lens.abstract: Color communication is more than a naming game where the informant names each color: the color terms must also be understood by the listener. Here, we studied how participants' productive and receptive vocabularies affect communication about color over the life span. Human participants, 3-72 years old, played a color communication game. lens.title: Engineering Vision: The Comparative Role of 3D Printing and 3D Bioprinting in Corneal Regeneration.
lens.summary: Corneal blindness remains a major global cause of vision loss, and the limited availability of donor tissue has intensified efforts to engineer functional corneal substitutes with appropriate optical, mechanical, and biological performance. …
lens.abstract: Corneal blindness remains a major global cause of vision loss, and the limited availability of donor tissue has intensified efforts to engineer functional corneal substitutes with appropriate optical, mechanical, and biological performance. Advances in additive manufacturing have positioned 3D printing and 3D bioprinting as promising platforms for fabricating anatomically informed constructs that may recapitulate key aspects of the cornea's hierarchical architecture. This review provides a mechanistic comparison of these technologies with respect to material systems and (bio)ink formulation, processing strategies, scaffold architecture, cell incorporation, and biological integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the trade-off between high-fidelity 3D-printed scaffolds that can be seeded after fabrication and cell-laden bioprinted constructs that better capture early cell-matrix inter

lens.title: Fixational saccades and drift parameters are altered in poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus: a pilot study.
lens.summary: UNLABELLED: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a prevalent metabolic condition associated with neuronal and vascular complications across multiple organ systems, including the eye, leading to vision impairment. Evidence suggests that structural and functional deficits may arise before funduscopically detectable changes in T2DM. …
lens.abstract: UNLABELLED: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a prevalent metabolic condition associated with neuronal and vascular complications across multiple organ systems, including the eye, leading to vision impairment. Evidence suggests that structural and functional deficits may arise before funduscopically detectable changes in T2DM. Fixational eye movements (FEMs) reflect the integrity of the oculomotor control systems and may serve as early functional markers of neurological dysfunction. FEM parameters in T2DM with good vision and without retinopathy have not been comprehensively characterized. Using a tracking scanning laser ophthalmoscope (TSLO) during a perimetry task, this pilot study characterizes FEM parameters in 43 age-matched participants stratified by hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c): controls (HbA1c < 5.7%; n = 18), prediabetes (HbA1c ≥ 5.7 and < 6.5%; n = 11), well-controlled T2DM (HbA1c ≥

lens.title: Two-strip scleral contraction for complex macular and peripapillary retinoschisis in pathologic myopia.
lens.summary: In this initial case series, the two-strip SC technique demonstrated preliminary anatomical success for combined macular and peripapillary retinoschisis over a 6-month observation period. No severe short-term complications were observed. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological myopia (PM) is a leading cause of visual impairment worldwide, often complicated by macular and peripapillary retinoschisis. This prospective pilot case series evaluated the technical feasibility, short-term anatomical outcomes, and observed complications of two-strip scleral contraction (SC) in eyes with concurrent macular retinoschisis (MRS) and peripapillary retinoschisis (PPRS). METHODS: In this prospective case series, 13 eyes with both macular and peripapillary retinoschisis confirmed by wide-field OCT were enrolled. All patients underwent two-strip SC, which involved placing two allogeneic dura mater strips over the macular and nasal peripapillary sclera to reduce axial length (AL). lens.title: Discovering a Novel AAV2-Based Capsid for RPE Transduction Via Intravitreal Injection for Leber Congenital Amaurosis Type 2 Gene Therapy.
lens.summary: Variant 3 is capable of RPE transduction with IVT injection, serving as a vehicle for less invasive IVT gene delivery to the RPE. Therapeutic gene delivery leads to functional results with efficiency limitations.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Several retinal degenerations initiate because of gene defects in the outermost retinal layer, the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Subretinal injection achieves optimal RPE transduction but has limitations, including iatrogenic damage. Here, we develop and evaluate the efficacy of a novel adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid with intravitreal delivery, in an effort to overcome limitations of subretinal delivery for treatment of retinal degenerations that require precise targeting of the outer retina. METHODS: We conducted a high-throughput screening of 1.28 × 109 AAV2 capsids, each with a different 7-mer peptide insertion to alter its binding properties, to be delivered with intravitreal (IVT) injection, a less invasive surgical procedure. lens.title: A critical review of the progress and application of finite element models in corneal biomechanics.
lens.summary: Corneal morphology and biomechanics are the primary determinants of visual quality. Accurate biomechanical characterization is essential for optimizing the outcomes of refractive surgery and managing pathologies such as keratoconus. …
lens.abstract: Corneal morphology and biomechanics are the primary determinants of visual quality. Accurate biomechanical characterization is essential for optimizing the outcomes of refractive surgery and managing pathologies such as keratoconus. Finite element modeling is an established method used to simulate surgical procedures, predict mechanical responses, and investigate pathological mechanisms. This review evaluates the progression of corneal finite element models. Early work relied on idealized two-dimensional cross-sections or simplified three-dimensional shapes; today, researchers routinely build personalized, high-resolution three-dimensional reconstructions directly from clinical image data. lens.title: Pressurized lacrimal duct irrigation for neonatal dacryocystitis: a pilot study of safety, effectiveness, and intervention timing.
lens.summary: The improved pressurized lacrimal duct irrigation technique for neonatal dacryocystitis was found to be safe and effective, with higher patency rates observed in infants aged 3-5 months.
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The study aims to assess the effectiveness, safety, and age-related outcomes of a pressurized lacrimal duct irrigation technique in neonatal dacryocystitis. METHODS: The study analyzed the outcomes of 145 infants (166 eyes) diagnosed with neonatal dacryocystitis at Affiliated Xiamen Eye Center of Xiamen University. Participants were categorized into three age-based cohorts: Group A (3-5 months), Group B (6-8 months), and Group C (9-11 months). A modified pressurized lacrimal duct irrigation technique was performed to unblock the lacrimal duct. The lacrimal duct patency and incidence of related complications were observed and recorded after the procedure. The infants were followed up for a week, and the procedure was repeated if the blockage persisted. lens.abstract: Fuchs' Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy (FECD), a degenerative corneal disorder, is marked by the thickening of Descemet's membrane and a progressive loss of corneal endothelial cells, ultimately leading to vision loss. A feature associated with the disease is the reduced stiffness of Descemet's membrane. However, the effects of this change in Descemet's membrane, on corneal endothelial cell health are not well understood. This study explored how changes in substrate stiffness and the signaling pathways associated with these changes influence corneal endothelial functions. In bovine corneal endothelial cells cultured on soft substrate, there was significant increase of p-FAK, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) markers, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. lens.title: Impact of soft contact lens power on lens fit.
lens.summary: For somofilcon-A daily-disposable silicone hydrogel lenses, with a fixed base curve and diameter, changing spherical power by up to ±2.00DS shows no statistically significant difference in SCL fitting characteristics. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine if a wider range of soft contact lens (SCL) can be more efficiently applied for fitting. This study evaluates whether altering spherical power by up to ±2.00 diopters (DS) within a single material and design changes on-eye fitting characteristics. METHODS: Prospective, randomised, cross-over, Open-label study was conducted. Each participant received either spherical Exact-Rx (current prescription) or Test lenses lens (±2.00DS to Exact-Rx; avoiding sign reversal) or toric Exact-Rx/Test lenses according to their refractive needs. After ≥15 min settling, centration (x/y decentration), corneal coverage, blink-induced movement, up-gaze and horizontal lag, push-up test, best-corrected distance visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR), and comfort, 1-10 scale and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), were measured. lens.title: Impact of Uncorrected Astigmatism on Image Quality With Dual-focus Optics-A Modelling Study.
lens.summary: The modelling shows that uncorrected astigmatism remains a major contributor to image degradation in eyes corrected with a DF contact lens, suggesting that astigmatic eyes being fitted with dual-focus or bifocal contact lenses would benefit from a toric correction.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Compare the impact of uncorrected astigmatism in a single-vision (SV) and a dual-focus (DF) optical lens models at the centre and limits of the interval of Sturm (IOS). METHODS: With the rule (WTR) astigmatism (up to 2.0 D) was added to SV and DF models. Wavefronts were constructed from Zernike polynomials over the full pupil (SV) or on a zone-by-zone basis (DF). The DF model included an annular zone with +2.0 D of added power and a typical decentration from the pupil centre. Geometrical ray tracing and wave optics were used to compute point-spread functions (PSF), modulation transfer functions (MTF) and simulated letter images at the centre, anterior and posterior limits of the IOS. lens.title: Acute idiopathic blind spot enlargement syndrome in a patient with high myopia: A case report with multimodal imaging findings.
lens.summary: RATIONALE: To report the clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging features, and treatment outcomes of a case of acute idiopathic blind spot enlargement syndrome (AIBSES) in a patient with high myopia. …
lens.abstract: RATIONALE: To report the clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging features, and treatment outcomes of a case of acute idiopathic blind spot enlargement syndrome (AIBSES) in a patient with high myopia. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 47-year-old male with high myopia presented with sudden visual field (VF) obscuration and photopsia in the left eye, with best-corrected visual acuity of 0.05 in the affected eye at initial examination. DIAGNOSES: Based on characteristic VF findings showing diffuse central sensitivity depression with a temporal defect contiguous with the physiological blind spot, optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing heterogeneous reflectivity of the neurosensory retina and focal discontinuity of the ellipsoid zone (EZ) signal, and multifocal electroretinography demonstrating reduced P1 response amplitude density across all 5 tested rings, a diagnosis of AIBSES was established. lens.title: [Research advances on the role of extracellular matrix alterations in the occurrence and progression of diabetic retinopathy].
lens.summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus and seriously endangers patients' visual function. As a core structural component of the retinal microenvironment, the extracellular matrix (ECM) participates in the occurrence and progression of DR via regulating cell proliferation, migration, ap …
lens.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus and seriously endangers patients' visual function. As a core structural component of the retinal microenvironment, the extracellular matrix (ECM) participates in the occurrence and progression of DR via regulating cell proliferation, migration, apoptosis and other mechanisms. However, the systematic understanding of its mechanisms in DR remains quite limited. This review systematically summarizes the structural and functional characteristics, pathological changes, signaling regulatory pathways and therapeutic advances of ECM in DR. Combined with the latest progress in artificial intelligence and multi-omics technologies, it prospects the application prospects of ECM-targeted intervention strategies. This article aims to deepen the understanding of ECM function in DR and provide new theoretical ba

lens.title: [Modified surgical techniques for macular holes: evolution and introspection].
lens.summary: Macular hole surgery has evolved from the initial simple pars plana vitrectomy to procedures in which peeling of the internal limiting membrane (ILM) over the macular surface constitutes the core technique. …
lens.abstract: Macular hole surgery has evolved from the initial simple pars plana vitrectomy to procedures in which peeling of the internal limiting membrane (ILM) over the macular surface constitutes the core technique. In recent years, an increasing number of modified techniques have continued to emerge, including ILM flap inversion, ILM flap insertion, and transplantation of various biological materials. However, issues such as the unclear surgical indications of these modified techniques have prompted the academic community to reflect on the diversification of macular hole surgical approaches. Based on a systematic review of the rationale behind the evolution of macular hole surgical techniques, this article offers a critical appraisal of the advantages and disadvantages of each technique and advocates a precise surgical strategy guided by evidence-based medicine. lens.title: Cost-effectiveness of digital health in primary care: a systematic review.
lens.summary: Digital health in primary care demonstrated favourable economic outcomes across a broad range of clinical areas, with the majority of studies reporting cost-effective results. However, despite this positive pattern, methodological heterogeneity limits comparability between studies. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Digital health has rapidly expanded, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, and is widely used for consultations, disease management, and efficiency improvements in primary care. While it is considered clinically effective and potentially cost-effective, evidence on economic impact remains limited. Previous reviews have been condition-specific, highlighting the need for a systematic review focused on cost-effectiveness of digital health within primary care. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this systematic review was to summarize and investigate the cost-effectiveness of digital health among adult primary care patients. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted using the PICO framework. Studies were included if they involved adult primary care patients (≥18 years), evaluated digital health interventions versus usual care, and reported cost‑effectiveness based on economic eval

lens.title: Physiological aging of the tear film: characterizing non-invasive breakup time dynamics by age and sex.
lens.summary: Tear film stability decreases progressively with age and differs by sex, with females showing lower and more variable NITBUT. These findings support incorporating age- and sex-related factors into DED evaluation and management, and align with growing evidence that qualitative tear film changes contribute to age-related instability.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: This study assessed the relationship between age and non-invasive tear breakup time (NITBUT), and examined sex-related differences in NITBUT to identify age- and sex-specific patterns relevant to the risk and presentation of dry eye disease (DED). METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed clinical records of adults who underwent optical prescription fittings between 2016 and 2024. NITBUT was measured with the Nidek Corneal Analyzer OPD-Scan III in 570 subjects (287 males, 283 females) aged 21-69 years, with approximately six subjects per one-year age interval. Group comparisons and regression analyses assessed associations with age and sex. RESULTS: Mean NITBUT was 8.27 ± 2.15 s in males, 7.46 ± 2.45 s in females, and 7.86 ± 2.01 s overall, with males significantly longer than females (p < 0.001). lens.title: Volumetric Quantification of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs) in Coronary Artery Disease.
lens.summary: In this contemporary coronary angiography cohort with high-density OCT imaging, RIPL burden was not significantly associated with CAD and no robust or proportional association with CAD severity was found. In this work, no other disease specific associations could be established.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) have been reported as correlates of several systemic conditions. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, number, area, and volume of RIPLs and to evaluate their association with coronary artery disease (CAD) using a contemporary imaged coronary angiography (CA) cohort. METHODS: CA patients were imaged using an SS-OCTA device during the same visit. Structural volumes comprising 500 B-scans were pixel-wise annotated by three graders. RIPLs were quantified by presence, count, area and volume for the first time. CAD severity was assessed using the Gensini score (GS). Associations between RIPL metrics and CAD were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Multivariable and age and sex adjusted models were calculated. lens.title: Hypoosmolar riboflavin for corneal swelling in thin keratoconic corneas prior to crosslinking: An exploratory study.
lens.summary: In this exploratory study, most eyes with pachymetry <400 µm after induction with isoosmolar riboflavin achieved adequate corneal swelling with HORF, with no significant changes in CDVA or keratometry observed over follow-up. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Corneal crosslinking (CXL) treats progressive keratoconus (KCN), but thin corneas may fall below 400 µm after epithelial removal and riboflavin induction, risking endothelial damage. Hypoosmolar riboflavin ophthalmic solution (HORF) can swell corneas intraoperatively, though factors contributing to achieving adequate corneal swelling using HORF that allows for safe CXL remain undefined. OBJECTIVE: To explore the associations between preoperative and post-induction minimum corneal thickness (MCT) and the corneal swelling response to HORF in patients with thin keratoconic corneas undergoing CXL. DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center consecutive case series. METHODS: Keratoconic eyes that dehydrated to <400 µm after isoosmolar riboflavin with 20% dextran and required HORF swelling prior to CXL were included. lens.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
lens.summary: In selected post-myopic LASIK eyes, expected DOFi-based functional differences remained evident after correction of residual refractive error. Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK showed generally comparable refractive performance. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare refractive predictability and functional visual outcomes among three depth-of-field (DOFi)-based intraocular lens (IOL) categories in eyes with previous myopic laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK). SETTING: A single-center, university-affiliated hospital. DESIGN: Retrospective comparative cohort study. METHODS: 90 eyes of 45 patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery after myopic LASIK were classified according to implanted IOL type: Full-DOFi Smooth (Tecnis Synergy), Partial-DOFi Enhanced (Eyhance), and Partial-DOFi Extended IOLs (PureSee). Distance-corrected visual acuity, monocular distance-corrected defocus curves, DOFi at 0.2 logMAR, refractive predictability with Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK after IOL-specific optimization or mean prediction error zeroing, and patient-reported satisfaction were evaluated 3 months postoperatively. lens.title: 27-gauge microincision vitrectomy for acute nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy with peripapillary wrinkles: a pilot study.
lens.summary: 27-gauge MIVS may be associated with visual benefits for acute NAION patients with PPWs. The favorable short-term safety profile and exploratory structural observations, coupled with potential functional benefits, warrants further investigation in larger randomized trials to confirm the role of MIVS in this subgroup.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: To assess the functional stabilizing potential and structural safety of 27-gauge microincision vitrectomy surgery (MIVS) in a targeted subgroup of patients with acute nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) presenting with peripapillary wrinkles (PPWs). METHODS: In this prospective, nonrandomized, patient-choice controlled pilot study, 39 patients presenting with acute unilateral NAION and PPWs (within 21 days of onset) were allocated into a surgical group (27-gauge MIVS) and a medical control group (tapered oral prednisone). All participants additionally received oral methylcobalamin. Main outcome measures included changes from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), mean deviation (MD), and visual field index (VFI); clinically meaningful response rates (≥ 15-letter BCVA gain/loss, ≥ 10% VFI, ≥ 3 dB MD change); and structural integrity of the foveal

lens.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
lens.summary: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confo …
lens.abstract: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confocal microscopy. Despite the wide diffusion of digital cameras, smartphones, and high-end slit-lamp systems, ocular surface photography (OSP) remains hampered by the absence of standardised acquisition and processing protocols. The convex, aspheric geometry of the ocular surface, off-axis illumination, peripheral defocus, automatic colour correction, and pupil-driven exposure variation in retroillumination limit reproducibility, inter-device comparability, and clinical utility. lens.title: Reduced magnocellular-biased visual responses are associated with working memory and linguistic difficulties in Chinese developmental dyslexia: A hypothesized visual-cognitive cascade.
lens.summary: Developmental dyslexia (DD) affects 5-10% of children worldwide. Although phonological theories predominate, they may not fully explain reading difficulties in orthographically dense scripts such as Chinese. …
lens.abstract: Developmental dyslexia (DD) affects 5-10% of children worldwide. Although phonological theories predominate, they may not fully explain reading difficulties in orthographically dense scripts such as Chinese. We investigated whether Chinese children with DD exhibit differences in early visual cortical responses and how these differences relate to reading-related skills. Steady-state visual evoked potentials (ssVEPs) were recorded from 50 children with DD and 50 typically developing controls aged 7-11 years using gratings that preferentially bias magnocellular or parvocellular processing. Global motion perception, visuospatial attention, verbal working memory, and linguistic skills were also assessed. lens.title: Perceived Challenges, Barriers, and Strategies for Orthokeratology Practice: Insights From Eye Care Practitioners in India.
lens.summary: The clinical adoption of Ortho-K among practitioners in India remains limited, with educational, infrastructural, and economic factors perceived as barriers to its wider integration. …
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the perceived challenges, barriers, and strategies associated with orthokeratology (Ortho-K) practice among eye care practitioners in India. METHODS: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based survey was conducted among eye care practitioners across India between November 2025 and February 2026. The survey assessed perceived challenges, barriers, and strategies related to Ortho-K practice using a five-point Likert scale. Responses were summarized using frequencies, percentages, and medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs). Differences in domain scores according to Ortho-K exposure were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, whereas correlations between domains were evaluated using Spearman rank correlation. lens.title: Delivery of atropine complexed with hydroxypropyl beta-cyclodextrin via a contact lens.
lens.summary: These findings support the stability and safety of atropine base formulations for potential ocular drug delivery.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Myopia is a global vision problem linked to a significant economic burden and potential blindness in severe cases. Current interventions-including atropine eye drops, contact lenses, spectacles, and lifestyle changes-are often combined due to limited individual effectiveness. This study aimed to develop and stabilize atropine formulations, load them into contact lenses, and evaluate atropine release profiles. METHODS: Atropine sulfate was converted to atropine base and complexed with 2-hydroxypropyl beta-cyclodextrin (HPBCD) in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at pH 6.5 or 7.4. Formulation stability was monitored over one year at room temperature (21°C) using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). lens.title: Macular Choroidal Thickness in Unilateral Idiopathic Epiretinal Membrane: A Fellow-Eye-Controlled Cross-Sectional Study.
lens.summary: Reduced macular choroidal thickness is associated with unilateral idiopathic ERM. Owing to the cross-sectional design, these findings demonstrate an anatomical association rather than a predictive or causal relationship. Prospective longitudinal studies are required to determine whether choroidal thinning precedes ERM development.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Idiopathic epiretinal membrane (ERM) is a prevalent cause of visual impairment among the elderly population. Given its uncertain pathogenesis, identifying anatomical factors associated with ERM may provide valuable insights into its clinical management. METHODS: Each patient diagnosed with unilateral idiopathic ERM underwent a complete ophthalmic examination. The results of fundus examinations were utilized to divide the eyes into two groups: ERM (+) and ERM (-). Macular retinal and choroidal thickness measured by swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) was evaluated to compare idiopathic ERM eyes with healthy fellow eyes. RESULTS: In this fellow-eye-controlled cross-sectional study, a total of 298 eyes from 149 patients with unilateral idiopathic ERM (mean age 58.42 ± 9.02 years) were analyzed. lens.title: Evening Blue Light Exposure, Ocular Growth Stimulation and Altered Dopamine.
lens.summary: Blue evening light reduced vitreal DOPAC levels, indicative of reduced retinal dopamine release, suggesting a dopamine-mediated mechanism in the blue-light-induced ocular growth stimulation. Choroidal dopamine may supplement retinal dopamine release in regulating eye growth.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Exposure to blue light in the evening stimulates eye growth at 200 but not 1000 lux. We asked whether the diurnal rhythm in retinal dopamine release is altered by evening blue light, whether the lack of effect at 1000 lux is due to higher dopamine, and whether the choroid may be a source of dopamine. METHODS: Chicks, on a 12h light-dark cycle with lights on at zeitgeber time 0 (ZT 0), were exposed to narrow-band blue light at 600 lux in the evening (ZT 8-ZT12) for 7d; control subjects were exposed to white light at 588 lux from ZT0 - ZT12. Eyes were dissected at 4-h intervals over 20 h, and the vitreous processed for dopamine (DA) and its metabolite DOPAC using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC).
